card.title: Manufacture of sulphuric acid by contact process

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The Contact process makes the king of acids in four stages: burn sulphur to SO₂, purify the gas exhaustively for the V₂O₅ catalyst's sake, oxidise 2SO₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2SO₃ at 450 °C and barely any pressure (the equilibrium is already ~99% converted — the deliberate contrast with Haber's bought pressure), and absorb the SO₃ in 98% acid to oleum because direct water would boil off an uncondensable fog.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - S + O₂ → SO₂; 2SO₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2SO₃ (V₂O₅, 450 °C, ΔH = −196 kJ/mol) - H₂SO₄ + SO₃ → H₂S₂O₇ (oleum); H₂S₂O₇ + H₂O → 2H₂SO₄

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Covers only: manufacture of sulphuric acid by contact process (within Modern Chemical Manufactures).  ·  Out of scope here: topics of neighbouring units in Chemistry — don't mix them.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: The absorbing medium's vapour pressure matters as much as its reactivity.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***The fog problem*** - SO3 into water gives an acid mist that cannot be condensed; SO3 into 98% acid gives oleum, a controlled intermediate - chemistry right, engineering wrong, fixed by diluent choice.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Contact Process: The King of Acids Sulphuric acid is made by the **Contact process**: sulphur (or pyrite) is burned to SO₂, the SO₂ is oxidised to SO₃ over a vanadium(V) oxide catalyst, and the SO₃ is absorbed in concentrated H₂SO₄ to give oleum, diluted to the commercial 98% acid.…  ·  ## 2. Theorem Mirror - **Step 1 — SO₂ generation:** S + O₂ → SO₂ (burning sulphur), or from pyrite: 4FeS₂ + 11O₂ → 2Fe₂O₃ + 8SO₂. - **Step 2 — purification (before the catalyst):** dust chamber → scrubber/washing tower → drying tower (conc. H₂SO₄) → **arsenic remover** — the gases must be clean because As and dust **poison the V₂O₅ catalyst**.…

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Pressure is purchased only when the pressureless equilibrium is too low - Contact's 99% needs none, Haber's 15% demands it.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Step 1: S + O2 -> SO2 (or 4FeS2 + 11O2 -> 2Fe2O3 + 8SO2). Step 2 purification: dust -> scrubber -> drying (conc. H2SO4) -> arsenic remover - protects the catalyst from poisoning.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: The purification train exists for the catalyst - arsenic and dust would poison the V2O5 and stop the plant.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 3. Deep Conceptual — Why Oleum and Not Water: The Fog Problem - Absorbing SO₃ directly into water is thermodynamically fine but **engineering-wise a disaster:** the reaction is violently exothermic and the product leaves the gas–liquid interface as a **mist of tiny H₂SO₄ droplets** that is nearly impossible to condense — it escapes with the exit gas as acid fog.…  ·  ## 4. Deep Conceptual — Why the Pressure Is Low: Reading an Equilibrium Economically - 2SO₂ + O₂ → 2SO₃ reduces 3 mol to 2 mol, so pressure *does* favour the product — yet the plant runs at **1–2 atm**. The reason: at 450 °C with excess air the equilibrium conversion is already ~99% without added pressure, and pressure equipment for a marginal 1% is uneconomic.…  ·  ### Deep dive — the contact process: why the absorber absorbs into acid, not water S (or FeS₂/pyrite) → SO₂ (roaster or burner) → SO₃ over V₂O₅ catalyst at ~450 °C, 1–2 atm (2SO₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2SO₃, ΔH = −196 kJ, exothermic and mole-reducing, so moderate T and slight pressure) → absorption.…
